posts.description:
Super excited to have placed 3rd at the HBS Tech Club's AI Hackathon this past weekend alongside Yvonne Yan, CFA and Cindy Phuong!

Challenged to build a consumer-focused product with real business potential, we created TripBlend - a "Spotify playlist blend" but for group trip planning.

TripBlend gathers basic parameters (location, dates, budget), and hyper-personalized preferences from social media integrations, to create a trip itinerary that the whole group will love. We also envisioned a monetization model using a virtual credit card, that serves users by making splitting trip expenses super easy.

Check out our prototype here: https://lnkd.in/gGSHm7RM

Huge thank you to the Tech Club at Harvard Business School for hosting, and Lovable & Kalodata for sponsoring this fun day!

Last Saturday, I went to an NVIDIA warm-up event for GTC Berlin and drank beer brewed by AI agents. 🦞🍺

Gerhard runs Lobster Lager. Agents built his website and handle the logistics, the ingredients, the recipes and the brewing. What they still haven't automated: taxes. Very German.

His line stuck with me: "If I, at 68, can use this, imagine what you could be doing."

As a DevRel, I was just as hooked on how Mark Heaps ran the room. He turned every transition into a story, brought a bit of Texas to Berlin, and never pitched once. He put builders on stage and let them do the inspiring. Honestly, a masterclass in developer storytelling.

Want to build something yourself? Here are some free resources from the event:
- Build-a-Claw Resource Hub: https://lnkd.in/dyk89aAK
- Free NemoClaw & OpenShell course: https://lnkd.in/dChQ6_tG
- NVIDIA NemoClaw GitHub: https://lnkd.in/dfDSdNKR

Cheers!

Excited to share that I’ll be attending SC26 (Supercomputing 2026) in Chicago next week, my first academic conference!

I’ll be presenting our poster, "Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication on Cerebras WSE-3," alongside Zenchang Sun and Arman Margarian.

Our work explores how to efficiently implement sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine, leveraging its massively parallel architecture to accelerate sparse computation at scale.

I’m incredibly grateful to Professor Giulia Guidi for her mentorship and guidance throughout this project, and to everyone at the ALPS Research Lab for their support and collaboration.

Looking forward to sharing our work, learning from the HPC community, and making new connections at SC26!

Poster: https://lnkd.in/eDuEUqJm

#SC26 #HPC #Supercomputing #Cerebras

posts.description:
ClarityCare announced a $16.5 million Series A led by Headline.
Its AI agent, Electra, handles prior authorization paperwork for health plans and can approve or escalate requests for human review.

A request may start in a fax inbox, pass through a clinical review queue, and end with a letter to a provider. ClarityCare says Electra can now create cases in a health plan’s utilization management system and send letters and faxes to close them. It checks clinical guidelines and member benefits, keeps an audit trail, and leaves denials to human reviewers.

ClarityCare AI plans to use the funding to grow its team, build new products, and expand its work in government healthcare. As Electra takes on more of the workflow, one measure of progress will be how quickly the hard cases reach a clinician with the information needed to make a decision.

Quick facts👇
● founders: Hermine T.; Alexandru Andrei
● total capital raised: nearly $20 million
● HQ: San Francisco, California
● Investors: Headline; Arthur Ventures; FJ Labs; Maverick Ventures; firstminute capital; Top Harvest Capital; Transpose Platform; Entrepreneurs First

posts.description:
We placed 4th at the YC x Naïve Hackathon and created Claim OS, a fully autonomous company that appeals homeowners property taxes for them.

View our demo here: https://lnkd.in/g8k5MXMd

Coming from the DMV, we've noticed that although many homeowners' properties are over assessed, very few (<5%) appeal. The appeal process is tedious and can be expensive to hire human tax agents, so many people put it off and overpay.

The challenge of the hackathon was to build a company that runs entirely on AI agents, using Naïve. So, we built Claim OS to file property tax appeals for homeowners, run entirely by agents.

As my first hackathon, this was an incredibly fun event. Great working with my teammates Nick Dev, Francesco Rosciano, and Tarang Goyal and thank you to Y Combinator, Naïve, AgentMail (YC S25), and Monid for making this event possible and for the credits!

Comment your feedback and thoughts!

#yc #hackathon #naive

🏆 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗮 𝘁𝗼 𝟭𝘀𝘁 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝗿𝗶𝘀 𝗛𝗮𝗰𝗸𝘀 𝗜𝗩. Here’s the story of 𝗠𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘆.

Hackathons have a funny way of turning one uncomfortable question into something real.

Ours was simple:
𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝗳 𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝘂𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗯𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗸𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗽𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗲?

Imagine an AI agent issuing an $850 refund without approval. Its response might sound perfectly reasonable but the action itself is a serious failure.

We decided to build something that could 𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗳𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘂𝗿𝗲, 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝘀𝗶𝗹𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻.

That became 𝗠𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘆, an open-source behavioral fuzz-testing engine for AI agents.

🔍 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗱𝗶𝗱 𝘄𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱?
• Automated adversarial conversations to uncover unsafe agent behavior.
• Deterministic policy checks against actual tool calls not just generated text.
• Minimal, reproducible failure cases saved as regression tests.
• A Python CLI and an OpenAI Agents SDK integration to help developers test their own agents.

The workflow: 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘃𝗶𝗼𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 → 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝘁 → 𝗙𝗶𝘅 𝗶𝘁 → 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀.

And the result?
🥇 𝟭𝘀𝘁 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗮𝘁 𝗜𝗿𝗶𝘀 𝗛𝗮𝗰𝗸𝘀 𝗜𝗩!

But the win is only one milestone. We're building Mutiny into something developers can actually use, extend and improve together.

💻 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁:
🔗 GitHub: https://lnkd.in/g-_R9Ci2

🏆 Winning submission: https://lnkd.in/gRghWnz3

📦 Install: https://lnkd.in/gWbJsP3p

The repository already has 𝟭𝟬+ 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀, and we're open to more!

If you're into Python, AI agents, backend engineering, testing or open source, check out our issues and contribute.

Because AI safety shouldn't depend on an agent simply saying, “Trust me, I followed the rules.” 😅

𝗟𝗲𝘁'𝘀 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗶𝘁.

𝗔 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗸 𝘆𝗼𝘂 to Iris Hacks for organizing the hackathon and Featherless AI for supporting the event with AI credits.
